fluff.name: Rogue
entries: Stealthy killers who are defined by their ability to hit enemies where it will cause the most damage. Rogues used honed skill and quick hands to approach, kill, and retreat before the target can respond.

weapons: Martial weapons that have the Finesse or Light property

entries: {@i Choose A or B:} (A) {@item Leather Armor}, 2 {@item Dagger|Daggers}, {@item Shortsword}, {@item Shortbow}, {@item Arrows (20)|20 Arrows}, {@item Quiver}, {@item Thieves' Tools}, {@item Burglar's Pack}, and 8 GP; or (B) 100 GP

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@rule Expertise} in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. {@skill Sleight of Hand} and {@skill Stealth} are recommended if you have proficiency in them.
At Rogue level 6, you gain {@rule Expertise} in two more of your skill proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Sneak Attack
entries: You know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra {@damage 1d6} damage to one creature you hit with an attack roll if you have {@rule Advantage} on the roll and the attack uses a Finesse or a Ranged weapon. The extra damage's type is the same as the weapon's type.

You don't need {@rule Advantage} on the attack roll if at least one of your allies is within 5 feet of the target, the ally doesn't have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition, and you don't have {@rule Disadvantage} on the attack roll.
The extra damage increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Rogue Features table.

classFeature.name: Thieves' Cant
entries: You picked up various languages in the communities where you plied your roguish talents. You know Thieves' Cant and one other language of your choice, which you choose from the language tables in Choose Languages.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the {@rule weapon mastery properties|mastery properties} of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as {@item Dagger|Daggers} and {@item Shortbow|Shortbows}.

Whenever you finish a {@rule Long Rest}, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose. For example, you could switch to using the {@rule weapon mastery properties|mastery properties} of {@item Scimitar|Scimitars} and {@item Shortsword|Shortswords}.

classFeature.name: Cunning Action
entries: Your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. On your turn, you can take one of the following actions as a {@rule Bonus Action}: {@action Dash}, {@action Disengage}, or {@action Hide}.

classFeature.name: Rogue Subclass
entries: You gain a Rogue subclass of your choice. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Rogue levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Rogue level or lower.

classFeature.name: Steady Aim
entries: As a {@rule Bonus Action}, you give yourself {@rule Advantage} on your next attack roll on the current turn. You can use this feature only if you haven't moved during this turn, and after you use it, your {@rule Speed} is 0 until the end of the current turn.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Rogue levels 8, 10, 12, and 16.

classFeature.name: Cunning Strike
entries: You've developed cunning ways to use your Sneak Attack. When you deal Sneak Attack damage, you can add one of the following Cunning Strike effects. Each effect has a die cost, which is the number of Sneak Attack damage dice you must forgo to add the effect. You remove the die before rolling, and the effect occurs immediately after the attack's damage is dealt. For example, if you add the Poison effect, remove {@dice 1d6} from the Sneak Attack's damage before rolling.
If a Cunning Strike effect requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Poison (Cost: 1d6)
entries: You add a toxin to your strike, forcing the target to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the target has the {@condition Poisoned} condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of its turns, the {@condition Poisoned} target repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success.
To use this effect, you must have a {@item Poisoner's Kit} on your person.

entries.name: Trip (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If the target is Large or smaller, it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or have the {@condition Prone} condition.

entries.name: Withdraw (Cost: 1d6)
entries: Immediately after the attack, you move up to half your {@rule Speed} without provoking {@action Opportunity Attack|Opportunity Attacks}.

classFeature.name: Uncanny Dodge
entries: When an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack roll, you can take a {@rule Reaction} to halve the attack's damage against you (round down).

classFeature.name: Expertise
entries: You gain {@rule Expertise} in two of your Skill Proficiencies of your choice.

classFeature.name: Evasion
entries: You can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain dangers. When you're subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw and only half damage if you fail. You can't use this feature if you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition.

classFeature.name: Reliable Talent
entries: Whenever you make an ability check that uses one of your skill or tool proficiencies, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Improved Cunning Strike
entries: You can use up to two Cunning Strike effects when you deal Sneak Attack damage, paying the die cost for each effect.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Devious Strikes
entries: You've practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack deviously. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

entries.name: Daze (Cost: 2d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a {@rule Bonus Action}.

entries.name: Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw, or it has the {@condition Unconscious} condition for 1 minute or until it takes any damage. The {@condition Unconscious} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Obscure (Cost: 3d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw, or it has the {@condition Blinded} condition until the end of its next turn.

classFeature.name: Slippery Mind
entries: Your cunning mind is exceptionally difficult to control. You gain proficiency in Wisdom and Charisma saving throws.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the {@feat Ability Score Improvement} feat or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Subclass Feature
entries: You gain a feature from your Rogue Subclass.

classFeature.name: Elusive
entries: You're so evasive that attackers rarely gain the upper hand against you. No attack roll can have {@rule Advantage} against you unless you have the {@condition Incapacitated} condition.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an {@epic-boon |Epic Boon feat} or another {@feat |feat} of your choice for which you qualify. {@epic-boon Boon of the Night Spirit} is recommended.

classFeature.name: Stroke of Luck
entries: You have a marvelous knack for succeeding when you need to. If you fail a {@rule D20 Test}, you can turn the roll into a 20.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@rule Short Rest|Short} or {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Trickster
entries: {@i Enhance Stealth with Arcane Spells}

Some Rogues enhance their fine-honed skills of stealth and agility with spells, learning magical tricks to aid them in their trade. Some Arcane Tricksters use their talents as pickpockets and burglars, while others are pranksters.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to cast spells. See chapter 7 for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules as an Arcane Trickster.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: You know three cantrips: {@spell Mage Hand} and two other cantrips of your choice from the Wizard spell list (see that class's section for its list). {@spell Mind Sliver} and {@spell Minor Illusion} are recommended.
Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one of your cantrips, except {@spell Mage Hand}, with another Wizard cantrip of your choice.
When you reach Rogue level 10, you learn another Wizard cantrip of your choice.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

entries.name: Prepared Spells of 1st+ Level
entries: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose three level 1 Wizard spells. {@spell Charm Person}, {@spell Disguise Self}, and {@spell Fog Cloud} are recommended.

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Rogue levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Wizard spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the Arcane Trickster Spellcasting table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. For example, if you're a level 7 Rogue, your list of prepared spells can include five Wizard spells of level 1 or 2 in any combination.

entries.name: Changing Your Prepared Spells
entries: Whenever you gain a Rogue level, you can replace one spell on your list with another Wizard spell for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Wizard spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an {@item Arcane Focus} as a {@rule Spellcasting Focus} for your Wizard spells.

subclassFeature.name: Mage Hand Legerdemain
entries: When you cast {@spell Mage Hand}, you can cast it as a {@rule Bonus Action}, and you can make the spectral hand {@condition Invisible}. You can control the hand as a {@rule Bonus Action}, and through it, you can make Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks.

subclassFeature.name: Magical Ambush
entries: If you have the {@condition Invisible} condition when you cast a spell on a creature, it has {@rule Disadvantage} on any saving throw it makes against the spell on the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Versatile Trickster
entries: You gain the ability to distract targets with your {@spell Mage Hand}. When you use the Trip option of your Cunning Strike on a creature, you can also use that option on another creature within 5 feet of the spectral hand.

subclassFeature.name: Spell Thief
entries: You gain the ability to magically steal the knowledge of how to cast a spell from another spellcaster.

Immediately after a creature casts a spell that targets you or includes you in its area of effect, you can take a {@rule Reaction} to force the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw. The DC equals your spell save DC. On a failed save, you negate the spell's effect against you, and you steal the knowledge of the spell if it is at least level 1 and of a level you can cast (it doesn't need to be a Wizard spell). For the next 8 hours, you have the spell prepared. The creature can't cast it until the 8 hours have passed.
Once you steal a spell with this feature, you can't use this feature again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Assassin
entries: {@i Practice the Grim Art of Death}

An Assassin's training focuses on using stealth, poison, and disguise to eliminate foes with deadly efficiency. While some Rogues who follow this path are hired killers, spies, or bounty hunters, the capabilities of this subclass are equally useful for adventurers facing a variety of monstrous enemies.

subclassFeature.name: Assassinate
entries: You're adept at ambushing a target, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: You have {@rule Advantage} on {@rule Initiative} rolls.

entries.name: Surprising Strikes
entries: During the first round of each combat, you have {@rule Advantage} on attack rolls against any creature that hasn't taken a turn. If your Sneak Attack hits any target during that round, the target takes extra damage of the weapon's type equal to your Rogue level.

subclassFeature.name: Assassin's Tools
entries: You gain a {@item Disguise Kit} and a {@item Poisoner's Kit}, and you have proficiency with them.

subclassFeature.name: Infiltration Expertise
entries: You are expert at the following techniques that aid your infiltrations.

entries.name: Masterful Mimicry
entries: You can unerringly mimic another person's speech, handwriting, or both if you have spent at least 1 hour studying them.

entries.name: Roving Aim
entries: Your {@rule Speed} isn't reduced to 0 by using Steady Aim.

subclassFeature.name: Envenom Weapons
entries: When you use the Poison option of your Cunning Strike, the target also takes {@damage 2d6} Poison damage whenever it fails the saving throw. This damage ignores {@rule Resistance} to Poison damage.

subclassFeature.name: Death Strike
entries: When you hit with your Sneak Attack on the first round of a combat, the target must succeed on a Constitution saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}), or the attack's damage is doubled against the target.

subclassFeature.name: Inquisitive
entries: As an archetypal Inquisitive, you excel at rooting out secrets and unraveling mysteries. You rely on your sharp eye for detail, but also on your finely honed ability to read the words and deeds of other creatures to determine their true intent. You excel at defeating creatures that hide among and prey upon ordinary folk, and your mastery of lore and your keen deductions make you well equipped to expose and end hidden evils.

subclassFeature.name: Ear for Deceit
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you develop a talent for picking out lies. Whenever you make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check to determine whether a creature is lying, treat a roll of 7 or lower on the {@dice d20} as an 8.

subclassFeature.name: Eye for Detail
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check to spot a hidden creature or object or to make an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check to uncover or decipher clues.

subclassFeature.name: Insightful Fighting
entries: At 3rd level, you gain the ability to decipher an opponent's tactics and develop a counter to them. As a bonus action, you can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against a creature you can see that isn't {@condition incapacitated}, contested by the target's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. If you succeed, you can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage on it.
This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until you successfully use this feature against a different target.

subclassFeature.name: Steady Eye
entries: Starting at 9th level, you have advantage on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.

subclassFeature.name: Unerring Eye
entries: Beginning at 13th level, your senses are almost impossible to foil. As an action, you sense the presence of illusions, shapechangers not in their original form, and other magic designed to deceive the senses within 30 feet of you, provided you aren't {@condition blinded} or {@condition deafened}. You sense that an effect is attempting to trick you, but you gain no insight into what is hidden or into its true nature.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses of it when you finish a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Eye for Weakness
entries: At 17th level, you learn to exploit a creature's weaknesses by carefully studying its tactics and movement. While your Insightful Fighting feature applies to a creature, your Sneak Attack damage against that creature increases by {@damage 3d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Mastermind
entries: Your focus is on people and on the influence and secrets they have. Many spies, courtiers, and schemers follow this archetype, leading lives of intrigue. Words are your weapons as often as knives or poison, and secrets and favors are some of your favorite treasures.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Intrigue
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with the {@item disguise kit}, the {@item forgery kit}, and one {@item gaming set} of your choice. You also learn two languages of your choice.

Additionally, you can unerringly mimic the speech patterns and accent of a creature that you hear speak for at least 1 minute, enabling you to pass yourself off as a native speaker of a particular land, provided that you know the language.

subclassFeature.name: Master of Tactics
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can use the {@action Help} action as a bonus action. Additionally, when you use the {@action Help} action to aid an ally in attacking a creature, the target of that attack can be within 30 feet of you, rather than within 5 feet of you, if the target can see or hear you.

subclassFeature.name: Insightful Manipulator
entries: Starting at 9th level, if you spend at least 1 minute observing or interacting with another creature outside combat, you can learn certain information about its capabilities compared to your own. The DM tells you if the creature is your equal, superior, or inferior in regard to two of the following characteristics of your choice:
At the DM's option, you might also realize you know a piece of the creature's history or one of its personality traits, if it has any.

subclassFeature.name: Misdirection
entries: Beginning at 13th level, you can sometimes cause another creature to suffer an attack meant for you. When you are targeted by an attack while a creature within 5 feet of you is granting you cover against that attack, you can use your reaction to have the attack target that creature instead of you.

subclassFeature.name: Soul of Deceit
entries: Starting at 17th level, your thoughts can't be read by telepathy or other means, unless you allow it. You can present false thoughts by succeeding on a Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check contested by the mind reader's Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check.
Additionally, no matter what you say, magic that would determine if you are telling the truth indicates you are being truthful if you so choose, and you can't be compelled to tell the truth by magic.

subclassFeature.name: Phantom
entries: {@i Embrace Death and Wield Ghostly Power}

Some Rogues traverse the veil between life and death, shepherding opponents to the grave and slipping through the world as undetectable as a spirit. In these pursuits, a Rogue might discover a mystical connection to death itself. Such an individual becomes immersed in negative energy, infusing their strikes with deathly energy and stealing knowledge from souls who have passed on. Thieves' guilds value Rogues of this persuasion as highly effective information gatherers and spies.

subclassFeature.name: Wails from the Grave
entries: Immediately after you deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature on your turn, you can target a second creature that you can see within 30 feet of the first creature. Roll half the number of Sneak Attack damage dice for your level (round up), and the second creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total as wails of the dead sound around it.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Dexterity modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Whispers of the Dead
entries: Whenever you finish a {@rule Short Rest|Short} or {@rule Long Rest}, you can choose one skill or tool proficiency that you lack and gain it, as a ghostly presence shares its knowledge with you. You lose this proficiency when you use this benefit again to choose a different proficiency.

subclassFeature.name: Tokens of the Departed
entries: The spirits of the dead are drawn to you, and echoes of their past lives magically manifest as strange curios with resonant power.

You gain two soul trinkets. A soul trinket is a Tiny object (the DM determines the trinket's form or has you roll on the {@item Trinket|Trinkets table} in the Player's Handbook to generate it). If you move more than 30 feet from a trinket, the trinket immediately teleports to you, appearing somewhere on your person.

entries.name: Using Soul Trinkets
entries: You can use soul trinkets in the following ways:

items.name: Death's Knell
items.entry: When you deal Sneak Attack damage on your turn, you can destroy one soul trinket and immediately use Wails from the Grave without expending a use of that feature.

items.name: Life Essence
items.entry: While you have at least one soul trinket, you have {@rule Advantage} on {@rule Death Saving Throw|Death Saving Throws} and Constitution saving throws.

items.name: Spirit Query
items.entry: You can take a {@action Magic} action to destroy one soul trinket and immediately cast the {@spell Augury} spell, requiring no spell components and using Constitution as the spellcasting modifier. If you know the creature with which the trinket is associated, you can ask the creature's spirit one question instead of casting the spell. In this case, the spirit appears to you and answers as concisely as possible in a language it knew in life.

entries.name: Gaining Additional Soul Trinkets
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you dies, you can take a {@rule Reaction} to gain another soul trinket, claiming a sliver of that creature's departing spirit. The new trinket appears somewhere on your person.

You can have a maximum of two soul trinkets at a time. If you try to gain a soul trinket while at your maximum, one of your existing trinkets is immediately destroyed and replaced by the new trinket. The maximum number of soul trinkets you can have increases when you reach Rogue levels 13 (three trinkets) and 17 (four trinkets).
Whenever you finish a {@rule Long Rest} with fewer than two soul trinkets, you gain soul trinkets until you have two.

subclassFeature.name: Voice of Death
entries: You can cast {@spell Speak with Dead} once without a spell slot, requiring no spell components and using Dexterity as the spellcasting modifier. You regain the ability to cast it this way when you finish a Short or Long Rest.
When you cast the spell, you can target one of your soul trinkets from Tokens of the Departed instead of a corpse, allowing the spirit of the creature associated with the trinket to answer.

subclassFeature.name: Ghost Walk
entries: As a {@rule Bonus Action}, you assume a spectral form, gaining the benefits below for 10 minutes or until you end them (no action required). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest} unless you destroy one of your soul trinkets from Tokens of the Departed (no action required) to restore your use of it.

entries.name: Flight
entries: You gain a {@rule Fly Speed} of 10 feet and can hover.

entries.name: Hazy Form
entries: Attack rolls have {@rule Disadvantage} against you.

entries.name: Incorporeal Movement
entries: You can move through creatures and objects as if they were {@rule Difficult Terrain}, but you take {@damage 1d10} Force damage if you end your turn inside a creature or an object.

subclassFeature.name: Death's Friend
entries: Your association with death has become so close that you gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Death's Lament
entries: When you use Wails from the Grave, you can deal the feature's Necrotic damage to both the first and the second creature.

entries.name: Draw of Death
entries: When you roll {@rule Initiative}, you gain one soul trinket for your Tokens of the Departed if you have none remaining.

subclassFeature.name: Scion of the Three
entries: {@i Become a Gruesome Agent of Malice}

A Scion of the Three draws power from a group of malevolent gods known as the Dead Three: Bane, deity of tyranny; Bhaal, deity of violence and murder; and Myrkul, deity of death. While some Rogues of this subclass pledge themselves ardently to those three macabre gods, others find themselves thrust on this path by a curse. Either way, a scion's power manifests as various occult gifts, as well as an uncanny talent for striking and terrifying foes.

Scions of the Three are most common in Baldur's Gate, where the Dead Three have long competed for influence over mortal hearts. Underground cults to Bane, Bhaal, and Myrkul often count Scions of the Three among their most useful agents. Outside Baldur's Gate, secular thieves' guilds such as the Shadow Thieves of Amn or Xanathar's guild in Waterdeep might cautiously call on a Scion of the Three to undertake an especially violent contract.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodthirst
entries: When an enemy you can see within 30 feet of yourself takes damage and is {@status Bloodied} after taking that damage but not killed outright, you can take a {@rule Reaction} and {@rule Teleportation|teleport} to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of that enemy. You can then make one melee attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Allegiance
entries: Choose one of the Dead Three: Bane, Bhaal, or Myrkul. You gain {@rule Resistance} to one type of damage and the ability to cast a cantrip, as detailed in the table below; Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for this cantrip. When you finish a {@rule Long Rest}, you can change your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Strike Fear
entries: You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

entries.name: Terrify (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or it has the {@condition Frightened} condition for 1 minute. While the target is Frightened in this way, you have {@rule Advantage} on attack rolls against the target.
The {@condition Frightened} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Malevolence
entries: You radiate malignant power associated with one of the Dead Three. When you use Bloodthirst and teleport, each creature of your choice within 10 feet of either the space you left or your destination space (your choice) takes damage equal to your Intelligence modifier; the damage type is the same as the damage {@rule Resistance} granted by your choice in the Dread Allegiance feature. Damage dealt by this feature ignores {@rule Resistance}.

subclassFeature.name: Dread Incarnate
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cutthroat
entries: You regain one expended use of Bloodthirst when you finish a {@rule Short Rest}.

entries.name: Murderous Intent
entries: When you roll for your Sneak Attack damage, you can treat a roll of a 1 or 2 on the die as a 3.

subclassFeature.name: Scout
entries: You are skilled in stealth and surviving far from the streets of a city, allowing you to scout ahead of your companions during expeditions. Rogues who embrace this archetype are at home in the wilderness and among barbarians and rangers, and many Scouts serve as the eyes and ears of war bands. Ambusher, spy, bounty hunter—these are just a few of the roles that Scouts assume as they range the world.

subclassFeature.name: Skirmisher
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you are difficult to pin down during a fight. You can move up to half your speed as a reaction when an enemy ends its turn within 5 feet of you. This movement doesn't provoke opportunity attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Survivalist
entries: When you choose this archetype at 3rd level, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} and {@skill Survival} skills if you don't already have it. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of those proficiencies.

subclassFeature.name: Superior Mobility
entries: At 9th level, your walking speed increases by 10 feet. If you have a climbing or swimming speed, this increase applies to that speed as well.

subclassFeature.name: Ambush Master
entries: Starting at 13th level, you excel at leading ambushes and acting first in a fight.

You have advantage on initiative rolls. In addition, the first creature you hit during the first round of a combat becomes easier for you and others to strike; attack rolls against that target have advantage until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Sudden Strike
entries: Starting at 17th level, you can strike with deadly speed. If you take the {@action Attack} action on your turn, you can make one additional attack as a bonus action. This attack can benefit from your Sneak Attack even if you have already used it this turn, but you can't use your Sneak Attack against the same target more than once in a turn.

subclassFeature.name: Soulknife
entries: {@i Strike Foes with Psionic Blades}

A Soulknife strikes with the mind, cutting through barriers both physical and psychic. These Rogues discover psionic power within themselves and channel it to do their roguish work. As a Soulknife, your psionic abilities might have haunted you since childhood, revealing their full potential only as you experienced the stress of adventure. Or you might have sought out an order of psychic adepts and spent years learning how to manifest your power.

subclassFeature.name: Psionic Power
entries: You harbor a wellspring of psionic energy within yourself. It is represented by your Psionic Energy Dice, which fuel certain powers you have from this subclass. The Soulknife Energy Dice table shows the number of these dice you have when you reach certain Rogue levels, and the table shows the die size.

Any features in this subclass that use a Psionic Energy Die use only the dice from this subclass. Some of your powers expend a Psionic Energy Die, as specified in a power's description, and you can't use a power if it requires you to use a die when your Psionic Energy Dice are all expended.
You regain one of your expended Psionic Energy Dice when you finish a {@rule Short Rest}, and you regain all of them when you finish a {@rule Long Rest}.

entries.name: Psi-Bolstered Knack
entries: If you fail an ability check using a skill or tool with which you have proficiency, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the check, potentially turning failure into success. The die is expended only if the roll then succeeds.

entries.name: Psychic Whispers
entries: You can establish telepathic communication between yourself and others. As a {@action Magic} action, choose one or more creatures you can see, up to a number of creatures equal to your {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}, and then roll one Psionic Energy Die. For a number of hours equal to the number rolled, the chosen creatures can speak telepathically with you, and you can speak telepathically with them. To send or receive a message (no action required), you and the other creature must be within 1 mile of each other. A creature can end the telepathic connection at any time (no action required).
The first time you use this power after each {@rule Long Rest}, you don't expend the Psionic Energy Die. All other times you use the power, you expend the die.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Blades
entries: You can manifest shimmering blades of psychic energy. Whenever you take the {@action Attack} action or make an {@action Opportunity Attack}, you can manifest a {@item Psychic Blade} in your free hand and make the attack with that blade. The magic blade has the following traits:
See {@item Psychic Blade}.
The blade vanishes immediately after it hits or misses its target, and it leaves no mark if it deals damage.

After you attack with the blade on your turn, you can make a melee or ranged attack with a second psychic blade as a {@rule Bonus Action} on the same turn if your other hand is free to create it. The damage die of this bonus attack is {@damage 1d4} instead of {@damage 1d6}.

subclassFeature.name: Soul Blades
entries: You can now use the following powers with your Psychic Blades.

entries.name: Homing Strikes
entries: If you make an attack roll with your {@item Psychic Blade} and miss the target, you can roll one Psionic Energy Die and add the number rolled to the attack roll. If this causes the attack to hit, the die is expended.

entries.name: Psychic Teleportation
entries: As a {@rule Bonus Action}, you manifest a {@item Psychic Blade}, expend one Psionic Energy Die and roll it, and throw the blade at an unoccupied space you can see up to a number of feet away equal to 10 times the number rolled. You then teleport to that space, and the blade vanishes.

subclassFeature.name: Psychic Veil
entries: You can weave a veil of psychic static to mask yourself. As a {@action Magic} action, you gain the {@condition Invisible} condition for 1 hour or until you dismiss this effect (no action required). This invisibility ends early immediately after you deal damage to a creature or you force a creature to make a saving throw.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest} unless you expend a Psionic Energy Die (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Rend Mind
entries: You can sweep your Psychic Blades through a creature's mind. When you use your Psychic Blades to deal Sneak Attack damage to a creature, you can force that target to make a Wisdom saving throw ({@dc 8} plus your Dexterity modifier and {@rule Proficiency|Proficiency Bonus}). If the save fails, the target has the {@condition Stunned} condition for 1 minute. The {@condition Stunned} target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@rule Long Rest} unless you expend three Psionic Energy Dice (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Swashbuckler
entries: {@i Glide into Melee with Panache and Agility}

As a Swashbuckler, you focus on the art of the blade, bringing speed, elegance, and charm to your combat style—topped off with an exquisite flourish of panache. You excel in single combat, and your methods make a duel look like a flamboyant performance.

subclassFeature.name: Fancy Footwork
entries: You've learned how to land a strike and then slip away without reprisal. If you make a melee attack roll against a creature during your turn, that creature can't make {@action opportunity attack|Opportunity Attacks} against you for the rest of that turn.

subclassFeature.name: Rakish Audacity
entries: When you roll {@rule Initiative}, you can give yourself a bonus to the roll equal to your Charisma modifier.

You also gain an additional way to use your Sneak Attack: You don't need {@rule Advantage} on the attack roll to use your Sneak Attack against a creature if you are within 5 feet of it, no other creatures are within 5 feet of you, and you don't have {@rule Disadvantage} on the attack roll. All the other rules for Sneak Attack still apply to you.

subclassFeature.name: Panache
entries: You have practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

entries.name: Goad (Cost: 1d6)
entries: The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw, or until the end of its next turn, the target has {@rule Disadvantage} on attack rolls against targets other than you and can't make {@action opportunity attack|Opportunity Attacks} against targets other than you.

entries.name: Awe (Cost: 3d6)
entries: Each creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Charmed} condition until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Dashing Strikes
entries: You have practiced new ways to use your Sneak Attack. The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options.

entries.name: Invigorate (Cost: 2d6)
entries: Choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself. Until the end of that creature's next turn, whenever it makes an attack roll or a saving throw, it can roll {@dice 1d6} and add the number rolled to the attack roll or saving throw.

entries.name: Parrying Stance (Cost: 2d6)
entries: Roll {@dice 1d6}. Until the start of your next turn, you gain a bonus to your AC equal to the number rolled.

subclassFeature.name: Master Duelist
entries: Immediately after you use your Sneak Attack, you can make another attack against the same target, provided you are within 5 feet of it and no other creatures are within 5 feet of you.

subclassFeature.name: Thief
entries: {@i Hunt for Treasure as a Classic Adventurer}

A mix of burglar, treasure hunter, and explorer, you are the epitome of an adventurer. In addition to improving your agility and stealth, you gain abilities useful for delving into ruins and getting maximum benefit from the magic items you find there.

subclassFeature.name: Fast Hands
entries: As a {@rule Bonus Action}, you can do one of the following.

entries.name: Sleight of Hand
entries: Make a Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) check to pick a lock or disarm a trap with {@item Thieves' Tools} or to pick a pocket.

entries.name: Use an Object
entries: Take the {@action Utilize} action, or take the {@action Magic} action to use a magic item that requires that action.

subclassFeature.name: Second-Story Work
entries: You've trained to get into especially hard-to-reach places, granting you these benefits.

entries.name: Climber
entries: You gain a {@rule Climb Speed} equal to your {@rule Speed}.

entries.name: Jumper
entries: You can determine your jump distance using your Dexterity rather than your Strength.

subclassFeature.name: Supreme Sneak
entries: You gain the following Cunning Strike option.

entries.name: Stealth Attack (Cost: 1d6)
entries: If you have the {@action Hide} action's {@condition Invisible} condition, this attack doesn't end that condition on you if you end the turn behind {@rule Cover|Three-Quarters Cover} or {@rule Cover|Total Cover}.

subclassFeature.name: Use Magic Device
entries: You've learned how to maximize use of magic items, granting you the following benefits.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: You can attune to up to four magic items at once.

entries.name: Charges
entries: Whenever you use a magic item property that expends charges, roll {@dice 1d6}. On a roll of 6, you use the property without expending the charges.

entries.name: Scrolls
entries: You can use any {@item Spell Scroll}, using Intelligence as your spellcasting ability for the spell. If the spell is a cantrip or a level 1 spell, you can cast it reliably. If the scroll contains a higher-level spell, you must first succeed on an Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) check ({@dc 10} plus the spell's level). On a successful check, you cast the spell from the scroll. On a failed check, the scroll disintegrates.

subclassFeature.name: Thief's Reflexes
entries: You are adept at laying ambushes and quickly escaping danger. You can take two turns during the first round of any combat. You take your first turn at your normal {@rule Initiative} and your second turn at your {@rule Initiative} minus 10.
